agustinia:eswiki:4.title: Agustinia ligabuei (Antigua visión errónea de las placas)

facts.statement: Agustinia is a genus of sauropod dinosaur containing only one known species, Agustinia ligabuei.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, A. ligabuei, known from a single specimen that was recovered from the Lohan Cura Formation of Neuquén Province in Argentina.

facts.statement: Agustinia lived approximately 116 to 108 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: It lived about 116–108 million years ago, in the Aptian–Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: The genus name Agustinia honors Agustin Martinelli, a student who discovered the skeleton during the excavation.
facts.quote: The generic name Agustinia honors then-student Agustin Martinelli, who discovered the skeleton and was part of the excavation team of the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales.

facts.statement: Agustinia was first described by Jose Bonaparte in 1999.
facts.quote: It was first mentioned in an abstract written by Argentine paleontologist Jose Bonaparte, and published in a full paper in 1999.

facts.statement: Agustinia is known only from fragmentary remains including vertebrae from the back, hips, and tail.
facts.quote: Only fragmentary remains of Agustinia are known. These include fragments of vertebrae from the back, hips, and tail regions of the spinal column.

facts.statement: Fragments of the lower hind limb, including a fibula, tibia, and five metatarsals, were recovered.
facts.quote: Parts of the lower hind limb were also recovered, consisting of a fibula, tibia, and five metatarsals.

facts.statement: A recovered fibula measures approximately 895 mm in length.
facts.quote: A fibula (lower leg bone) has been recovered that is about 895 mm long.

facts.statement: Based on the length of the fibula, Agustinia is estimated to have been about 15 meters long.
facts.quote: When compared to the same bone in related dinosaurs, this indicates that Agustinia may have been about 15 m long.

facts.statement: Agustinia was initially thought to possess distinctive armor plates interpreted as vertical spikes and plates along its back.
facts.quote: Agustinia was known for its distinctive supposed armor plates, called osteoderms, initially interpreted as a series of wide, vertical spikes and plates down the center of its back, somewhat like the unrelated Stegosaurus.

facts.statement: Subsequent research determined that the supposed armor plates were likely fragments of ribs and hip bones rather than osteoderms.
facts.quote: Further study of the poorly preserved fossil material showed that these "plates" were in fact more likely to be fragments of ribs and hip bones.

facts.statement: The tibia of Agustinia was thinner than that of titanosaurs like Antarctosaurus or Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: The lower half of the tibia was thin when viewed from the front (anteroposterior), indicating that the tibia was thinner than that of titanosaurs such as Antarctosaurus or Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: Some authors consider Agustinia a nomen dubium due to its fragmentary nature and lack of distinctive characteristics.
facts.quote: Because of this, some authors have considered Agustinia a nomen dubium for being based on inadequate remains to compare with related dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Agustinia was originally classified in its own family, Agustiniidae, due to its supposed unusual armor.
facts.quote: Because of its supposedly unusual armor, Agustinia was originally assigned to its own family, Agustiniidae.

facts.statement: D'emic et al. (2009) classified Agustinia as Neosauropoda incertae sedis due to a lack of diagnostic features.
facts.quote: In contrast, D'emic et al (2009) concluded that no diagnostic features were present that would allow a classification within the Diplodocoidea or Titanosauria, and therefore classified Agustinia as Neosauropoda incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Bellardini et al. (2022) classified Agustinia as a rebbachisaurid within the Diplodocoidea.
facts.quote: A 2022 publication by Flavio Bellardini et al. found sufficient evidence to classify Agustinia as a rebbachisaurid within the Diplodocoidea, more derived than Amazonsaurus.

facts.statement: Lerzo et al. (2024) supported a rebbachisaurid position for Agustinia, suggesting affinities closer to Nigersaurinae within Khebbashia.
facts.quote: In their 2024 description of Campananeyen, Lerzo et al. also found support for a rebbachisaurid position of Agustinia, although their analysis favored affinities closer to the Nigersaurinae within Khebbashia.

facts.statement: Initially, Agustinia was considered an armored sauropod with plates and spikes that lived alongside other large herbivores like Ligabuesaurus and Limaysaurus and reached about 16 meters in length.
facts.quote: En un principio se lo consideró un saurópodo armado con placas y espinas que habitó junto con otros grandes herbívoros como el Ligabuesaurus y el Limaysaurus y llegó a medir unos 16 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Bonaparte proposed the new family Agustiniidae to include Agustinia because it shared characteristics with both diplodocoids and titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Debido a que compartiria características con los diplodocoides y los titanosáuridos, Bonaparte propuso una nueva familia para incluirlo llamada Agustiniidae.

facts.statement: A 2022 publication by Flavio Bellardini et al. found sufficient evidence to classify Agustinia as a rebbachisaurid.
facts.quote: Una publicación de 2022 de Flavio Bellardini et al. encontró evidencia suficiente para clasificar a Agustinia como un rebaquisáurido.

facts.statement: Agustinia was a quadrupedal herbivore like other known sauropods.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio, al igual que todos los saurópodos conocidos, era cuadrúpedo y herbívoro.

facts.statement: Only fragmentary remains of Agustinia are known.
facts.quote: De Agustinia sólo se conocen restos fragmentarios .

facts.statement: A perone bone measuring 895 millimeters in length was recovered from Agustinia.
facts.quote: Se ha recuperado un peroné, hueso de la parte inferior de la pierna, de unos 895 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Comparison with related dinosaurs suggests Agustinia may have reached a length of 15 meters.
facts.quote: En comparación con el mismo hueso de dinosaurios relacionados, esto indica que Agustinia pudo haber medido unos 15 metros de largo.

facts.statement: A fragmentary hip bone was tentatively identified as part of the ilium.
facts.quote: El hueso fragmentario de la cadera fue identificado tentativamente como parte del ilion.

facts.statement: Some authors consider Agustinia a nomen dubium because its remains are insufficient for comparison with related dinosaurs without its supposed distinctive armor.
facts.quote: Sin su supuesta armadura distintiva, algunos autores han considerado a Agustinia como un nomen dubium, basándose en que sus restos no son adecuados para compararlo con dinosaurios emparentados.

facts.statement: Later research questioned the interpretation of certain elements as osteoderms.
facts.quote: investigaciones posteriores han cuestionado la interpretación de estos elementos como osteodermos.

facts.statement: Detailed study of poorly preserved fossil material showed that the supposed "plates" were likely fragments of ribs and hip bones.
facts.quote: Un estudio más detallado del material fósil mal conservado mostró que estas "placas" eran, de hecho, más probablemente fragmentos de costillas y huesos de la cadera.

facts.statement: Histological analysis confirmed that the supposed osteoderms did not match the internal structure of other titanosaurian osteoderms.
facts.quote: Esta revaluación fue reafirmada posteriormente por histología.de los supuestos osteodermos, que no coinciden con la estructura interna de otros osteodermos titanosaurianos.

facts.statement: The name Agustinia was proposed in honor of the specimen's discoverer, Agustín Martinelli.
facts.quote: El nombre Agustinia fue propuesto en honor al descubridor del espécimen, Agustín Martinelli.

facts.statement: The name was changed to Agustinia in a major work published in 1999, which also introduced the family Agustiniidae.
facts.quote: Bonaparte cambió el nombre a Agustinia en un gran trabajo publicado en 1999, que también introdujo a la familia Agustiniidae.

facts.statement: Only one species, A. ligabuei, has been discovered, named in honor of philanthropist Dr. Giancarlo Ligabue who funded the expedition.
facts.quote: Solo se ha descubierto una especie, A. ligabuei, nombrada en honor al Dr. Giancarlo Ligabue, un filántropo que proporcionó el apoyo financiero a la expedición que recuperó los restos.

facts.statement: Agustinia fossils were found in the Lohan Cura Formation in Argentina and date to the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Los fósiles del Agustinia fueron recuperados de la Formación de Lohan Cura, en el Cerro El León, cerca de Picún Leufú, Provincia del Neuquén en Argentina, que datan de las épocas Aptiana y Albiana en el Cretáceo inferior.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, housed at the Municipal Museum "Carmen Funes" in Plaza Huincul, Argentina, includes three incomplete dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, ten caudal vertebrae, nine pieces considered osteoderms, most of the right tibia and ulna, and five articulated left metatarsals.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo se encuentra el Museo Municipal "Carmen Funes" en Plaza Huincul, Provincia del Neuquén, y llamado MCF-PVPH-110, representado por tres vértebras dorsales, seis sacras y diez caudales todas incompletas, nueve trozosconsiderados osteodermos, la mayor parte de la tibia y ulna derecha y cinco metatarsianos izquierdos articulados.

facts.statement: Initially, Agustinia was thought to possess a body armor with a series of broad, vertical points and plates on its back.
facts.quote: En un principio se pensó que poseía una armadura corporal con una serie de puntos amplios, verticales y placas en su espalda.

facts.statement: Later studies of poorly preserved fossil material showed that the bony "plates" were very likely fragments of rib and hip bones.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios posteriores del material fósil mal preservado de este animal han mostrado que las "placas" óseas en realidad muy probablemente fragmentos de los huesos de las costillas y de la cadera.

facts.statement: Agustinia was initially assigned to its own family, Agustiniidae, due to its unusual features.
facts.quote: A causa de sus rasgos insólitos, Agustinia al principio fue asignado a su propia familia, Agustiniidae.

facts.statement: Bonaparte noted that the four perpendicular laminae with the postspinal laminae are most similar to rebbachisaurids rather than titanosaurians.
facts.quote: Bonaparte indica que las cuatro láminas perpendiculares con las láminas del postespinal son lo más de largo posible más similares a los rebaquiosáuridos que a los titanosáuridos.

facts.statement: D'emic et al. concluded there were no diagnostic features to classify Agustinia within Diplodocoidea or Titanosauria, so they classified it as incertae sedis.
facts.quote: D'emic et al concluyeron que no hay características diagnósticas presentes que permitirían una clasificación dentro de Diplodocoidea o Titanosauria y, por lo tanto, clasificaron a Agustinia como incertae sedis.

facts.statement: A 2022 publication by Flavio Bellardini et al. found sufficient evidence to classify Agustinia as a rebbachisaurid within Diplodocoidea, more derived than Amazonsaurus.
facts.quote: Una publicación de 2022 de Flavio Bellardini et al. encontró evidencia suficiente para clasificar a Agustinia como un rebaquisáurido dentro de los Diplodocoidea, más derivado que Amazonsaurus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Agustinia is Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rebbachisauridae

facts.statement: Agustinia belongs to the family Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Rebbachisauridae

facts.statement: Agustinia is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Agustinia is Agustinia ligabuei.
facts.quote: Type species: Agustinia ligabuei

facts.statement: Agustinia lived from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Agustinia is known from the Lohan Cura Formation of the Early Cretaceous in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Agustinia se conoce de la Formación Lohan Cura del Cretácico Inferior de la provincia de Neuquén, Argentina.

facts.statement: Other dinosaurs, including the rebbachisaurid Comahuesaurus and the somphospondylid Ligabuesaurus, have been named from the same formation.
facts.quote: Otros dinosaurios, incluidos sus compañeros rebaquisáuridos Comahuesaurus y somfospondidlo Ligabuesaurus, también han sido nombrados a partir de la formación.

facts.statement: Remains of turtles, including two species of Prochelidella, are also known from the formation.
facts.quote: También se conocen restos de tortugas, entre ellas dos especies de Prochelidella.

facts.statement: Agustinia is difficult to classify due to its fragmentary nature, which exposes traits of both diplodocoid and titanosaurian sauropods.
facts.quote: Agustinia es difícil de clasificar debido a su naturaleza fragmentaria, y porque esto expone los rasgos tanto de saurópodos diplodócidos como de saurópodos titanosaurianos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Agustinia is a diplodocoid or titanosaurian based on conflicting vertebral features, as diplodocoids have compressed dorsal spines while titanosaurians have six sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Tanto titanosáuridos y diplodocoides tienen láminas preespinales y postespinales en las vértebras dorsales posteriores y las vértebras caudales próximas, pero solamente los diplodocoides tienen vértebras dorsales posteriores con las espinas dorsales craniocaudalmente comprimidas y solamente Euhelopus y los titanosáuridos tienen seis vértebras sacras.
